records.old: 8 lessons × 40 minutes = 320 minutes total
records.new: 8 lessons × 80 minutes (each a double period of 2 × 40) = 640 minutes total
records.why: All eight lessons are double periods of 80 minutes (2 x 40). 8 x 80 = 640 minutes, not 8 x 40 = 320. The phase minutes inside Lessons 5 and 7 and the new timing guides in the other lessons all add to 80 per lesson, so 8 x 80 = 640 is consistent.

records.old: No final capacity or paint figures are given: the puzzle stays open for later lessons.
records.new: No final capacity or paint figures are given: the puzzle stays open for later lessons. Suggested timing (80 minutes): Predict 10, Observe 30, Explain 15, Driving Question Board 10, Model Building 15.
records.group_headline: Per-phase timing was missing or too long (Lesson 1 added up to about 95 minutes, Lesson 8 to 85+); every double period now has a guide that adds to 80 minutes
records.why: Lesson 1 gave Observe 15 + 25 = 40 minutes but no time for the other four phases (prediction writing, a poster definition, DQB notes, group models with a gallery walk and exit ticket), which would run to about 95 minutes. A teacher cannot fit that into 80 minutes, so a timing guide adding to 80 is added and the two Observe parts are trimmed to match.

records.why: Observe trimmed from 40 to 30 minutes (Part A 10 min: measuring three sufurias and dividing; Part B 20 min) so the whole lesson fits 80 minutes.

records.old: Part B (about 25 min)
records.new: Part B (about 20 min)
records.why: Part B trimmed to 20 minutes. Objects should be collected before the lesson (the text already says so) so the sorting and checking fits.

records.new: The mystery of the capacity and paint remains open for later lessons. Suggested timing (80 minutes): Predict 10, Observe 35, Explain 15, Driving Question Board 10, Model Building 10.
records.why: No timing guide was given. Observe was 25 + 15 = 40 minutes, leaving 40 for four phases that each include writing and cold-calling; Observe is trimmed to 35 and a guide adding to 80 is added.

records.old: Part 1 (about 25 minutes)

records.why: No timing guide was given for a lesson with a six-step Observe task and a CER explanation; a guide adding to 80 minutes is added.

records.new: noting that all lengths double but they still need to find out what happens to area and volume. Suggested timing (80 minutes): Predict 8, Observe 40, Explain 15, Driving Question Board 7, Model Building 10.

records.new: Task 4 (digital zoom, about 8 minutes; if devices are scarce the teacher shows it once on one device):
records.why: Many Kenyan partner schools have few phones or tablets, and four tasks in 40 minutes is tight with large classes. Task 4 now has a time limit and a one-device teacher-demonstration option.

records.old: They then update the DQB and the class model.
records.new: They then update the DQB and the class model. Suggested timing (80 minutes): Predict 10, Observe 25, Explain 25, Driving Question Board 8, Model Building 12.

records.new: compare their final model with their Lesson 1 model, and complete the Driving Question Board. Suggested timing (80 minutes): Predict 10, Observe 30, Explain 20, Driving Question Board 10, Model Building 10.
records.why: Lesson 8 listed Observe 35 + Explain 20 + Model 10 = 65 minutes and left 15 for Predict and DQB, which is more than the other phases need on a sensible split. A guide adding to 80 is added and Observe trimmed to 30 (see the project record).

records.old: Project build and check (about 35 minutes).
records.new: Project build and check (about 30 minutes; to fit the time, groups use tins and boxes collected earlier or containers made before the lesson, and any cutting and gluing of cardboard is done in advance or as a take-home task).
records.group_headline: Building two similar containers from scratch, filling them and filming the steps cannot be done in 35 minutes in a large class; builds now start from ready-made or pre-made containers
records.why: Planning, measuring, cutting, assembling two containers, calculating, fill-and-pour and photographing every step is far more than 35 minutes, and a tight 80-minute lesson also has to hold the Final Explanation. Two defensible options exist (use found tins/boxes and pre-built cardboard, or give a separate project lesson); I chose the first. Teacher decides what materials and pre-lesson time your school really has.

records.new: (ratio 1695.6 / 502.4 = 3.375 = 1.5 x 1.5 x 1.5). Surface areas of closed containers (check cases): cubes 6 x 25 = 150 and 6 x 100 = 600 cm2 (ratio 4); cuboids 2(20 + 15 + 12) = 94 and 2(80 + 60 + 48) = 376 cm2 (ratio 4); cylinders 2 x 3.14 x 4 x 10 + 2 x 3.14 x 16 = 351.68 and 2 x 3.14 x 6 x 15 + 2 x 3.14 x 36 = 791.28 cm2 (ratio 2.25 = 1.5 x 1.5).
records.why: Step 4 asks learners to calculate surface area, and the Predict phase asks for the paint factor, but the teacher had answers only for volume. Checked by recomputing: 6 x 25 = 150; 6 x 100 = 600; 376/94 = 4; 351.68 x 2.25 = 791.28.

records.new: why L feeds far more than twice as many
records.why: This sentence is spoken to learners in Lesson 2 but gives away the 8 times result that they discover in Lesson 6. The wording now matches the unresolved puzzle.

records.old: Do not reveal 8.
records.new: Tell learners that, by Mama Achieng's count, the small sufuria fills about 6 plates of githeri. Do not reveal 8.
records.why: The Predict phase asks how much more the large sufuria holds than the small one 'S about 6 servings', but the 6 was never given to learners earlier. The teacher now states it so every learner predicts from the same figure.

records.old: Do not re-teach area; just refer to k^2 = 4 from Lesson 5.
records.new: Do not re-teach area; just refer to k^2 = 4 from Lesson 5. Name the limit of the model: we treated each sufuria as a perfect cylinder and ignored wall thickness and any slight taper of a real sufuria, so servings are 'about' values and a real sufuria may hold a little less.
records.why: Guideline 6 asks for the limits of a model to be stated. The cylinder model of a sufuria is never limited anywhere in the unit.

records.old: k x OA'; explanation
records.new: k x OA; explanation
records.why: The formula was written OA' = k x OA'. Everywhere else (Lessons 3 and 4) it is OA' = k x OA, where OA is the object distance. Fixed so teachers do not listen for a wrong statement.

records.old: Distribute sheets, rulers and pencils and check
records.new: Before the lesson, prepare each sheet: draw triangle ABC, choose O, mark A', B', C' so that OA' = 2 x OA, OB' = 2 x OB and OC' = 2 x OC, draw the image, then rub out O and the lines through the points. Support: pair a learner who finds ruler work hard (low vision or fine-motor needs) with a partner who holds the ruler while they direct the line, and accept an oral explanation of why the lines meet. Distribute sheets, rulers and pencils and check
records.why: The task needs sheets where the three lines really meet at O, but the teacher is not told how to make them. Also adds a lesson-specific support for learners who struggle with the drawing, so they can still show understanding.

records.old: Select two learners to read their paragraph;
records.new: Offer choices for showing understanding: a written paragraph, an annotated diagram with a short caption, or a short spoken or recorded explanation in English or Kiswahili (all assessed with the same checklist). Select two learners to read their paragraph;
records.why: The Final Explanation task had only one way to respond (a written paragraph). Guideline 12 asks for more than one way to show understanding.

records.old: A map of Lake Victoria on a 1:50,000 scale shows a small shape, but the real lake covers a huge area, so a 1 cm length
records.new: A map of Kisumu town drawn at a scale of 1:50,000 fits on one page, but the real town covers a huge area: 1 cm on the map is 500 m, yet 1 cm² on the map is 250,000 m² (25 hectares), so a 1 cm length
records.why: At 1:50,000, 1 cm is 500 m, so Lake Victoria (about 337 km long) would be about 6.7 m long on the map, not 'a small shape'. A town such as Kisumu does fit on one page (a 30 cm page is 15 km). Checked: 50,000 cm = 500 m; (500 m)^2 = 250,000 m^2 = 25 ha (1 ha = 10,000 m^2). This matches the Lesson 7 map station.
records.reference: Ordnance Survey, 'Understanding scale' map-reading guidance (1:50,000 scale: 1 cm = 500 m); SI/metric conversion 1 ha = 10,000 m2

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Calculates all ratios correctly, states that corresponding angles are equal and all sides are in a constant ratio, and explains clearly why rectangle C is not similar to A.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Calculates most ratios correctly and states the constant-ratio idea, with a small gap in explaining why C is not similar.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Relies on shape looking the same or on equal angles only, and does not use a constant ratio of sides.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Finds k from lengths and from OA'/OA, finds the centre O by joining corresponding points, and handles both k = 2 and k = 0.5 correctly.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Finds k correctly and applies it to lengths, with minor errors in describing the centre or the reduction.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Confuses k with the difference between lengths or cannot find the image lengths from k.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Uses A = 2 pi r h + pi r^2 and V = pi r^2 h with pi = 3.14 accurately, gets all ratios (4 and 8), and finds servings and costs correctly with units.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Uses the formulas correctly with one or two arithmetic or unit slips.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Uses the wrong formulas or cannot connect the calculated figures to the ratios.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Explains that quantities depend on one, two or three lengths, so they multiply by k, k^2 or k^3, and uses the cube, rectangle and cylinder evidence. Works backwards from an area factor to k.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: States k^2 and k^3 correctly with some evidence but a limited explanation of why.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Says area and volume simply double when lengths double.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Links capacity (8 times, about 48 servings against 6), paint (4 times, about KSh 80 against KSh 20) and price (KSh 120 = 2 x 60) to the scale factor, and explains the bargain per serving.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Explains capacity and paint with the correct factors but only partly explains the price or the bargain.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Gives a general answer without the factors or without using Mama Achieng's data.

records.why: CBE uses four levels (Exceeds, Meets, Approaches, Below Expectations) but the partner contract allows only three level fields and the printed headings are fixed by the template, so a Below Expectations level cannot be represented. Suggestion: teachers treat work that does not reach the 'Approaches' descriptor as Below Expectations, or the contract is extended later.

KICD check not possible: data/raw/curriculum_pdfs/Grade10_Mathematics_Curriculum.pdf is the CORE Mathematics design (Strand 2.0, 2.1 Similarity and Enlargement, 12 lessons) and does not cover Essential Mathematics. Differences seen against the Core text, which may simply be real Essential Mathematics differences: 8 outcomes (a-h) here against 6 (a-f); the note 'negative scale factor will not be included'; core competencies (here Digital literacy and Creativity 'networking skills', in Core Communication and Collaboration and Creativity); values (Core also lists Integrity); PCIs (Core lists Social Cohesion and ESD); the project here omits spheres; the key inquiry question here reads 'How is similarity and enlargement applied in real life?' against 'How are similarity and enlargement applied in day-to-day life?'. No KICD wording was changed. Teachers should compare with the Essential Mathematics Grade 10 curriculum design. Within the unit, all eight listed outcomes are taught (a: L1-2, b: L3, c: L4, d: L5, e-f: L6-7, g-h: L7-8) and assessed in the Final Explanation.
